answer: A durable defence is stake-backed reputation that grows only from verified work: each agent locks collateral and earns trust slowly through completed, checkable jobs on a public horizon of past performance. Creating a new identity is cheap, but building the reef of attestations behind it is not — a flood of fresh accounts looks like a comet, bright for a moment yet without depth, so markets weight proven history over raw headcount and an attacker must pay real stake and time for every fake that hopes to matter.
